official.deadline_central_display: January 15 (Regular Decision / Early Decision II); November 1 for Early Action / Early Decision I
official.deadline_note: Clark publishes these dates without a year label on its current pages; they recur each admissions cycle, so in the cycle now open (fall 2027 entry) they fall on 1 November 2026 (Early Decision I / Early Action) and 15 January 2027 (Early Decision II / Regular Decision). The International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form and the Global Scholars essay follow the same admission deadlines - one financial-aid page still labels its table 'fall 2025 admission', which is leftover wording rather than a different deadline.
official.application_cycle: Clark's current first-year admissions rounds: Early Decision I and Early Action - November 1; Early Decision II and Regular Decision - January 15
official.status_note: Clark's undergraduate admissions and financial assistance pages present these first-year rounds as the live application path, and its international financial aid FAQ still lists the Global Scholars Program Scholarship among the five merit scholarships open to international first-year students, with a separate essay required for it and for the Presidential Scholarship.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Clark publishes no tuition-coverage statement specific to the Global Scholars Program Scholarship. The closest published wording applies to international aid as a whole: 'We are not able to offer financial assistance to cover the full cost of attendance.' On the admissions page Clark adds: 'Because our resources are limited, we can't offer admission to international students who require full funding. Typically, international students pay around $40,000 per year after considering scholarships and aid.'
benefits: Each year a select number of first-year and transfer international students receive merit scholarships and need-based grants to attend Clark - reflecting the university's recognition of the importance of diversity and strong global commitment.

All international first-year students are automatically considered for the International Traina Scholarship, the International Achievement Scholarship and the International Jonas Clark Scholarship; separate essays are required for the Presidential Scholarship and the Global Scholars Program Scholarship.
Merit scholarship decisions are made without consideration of financial need.
Admitted students who receive a merit-based scholarship will be notified at the time of admission.
eligibility: You are an international student if you are not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident.

Currently, international first-year students are eligible for five merit scholarships: the International Traina Scholarship, the International Achievement Scholarship, the International Jonas Clark Scholarship, the Presidential Scholarship and the Global Scholars Scholarship.
Separate essays are required to be considered for the Presidential Scholarship and the Global Scholars Program Scholarship.
Applying as a first-year undergraduate to Clark University by the Early Action / Early Decision (November 1) or Regular Decision (January 15) deadline.
All international students must complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form located on the Applicant Status Portal.

Our admissions process is need-aware, meaning that we will deny an application on financial grounds if the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form indicates greater need than we will be able to provide through merit scholarships and need-based financial aid.
SAT and ACT scores are optional for all students, including international applicants.
requirements: Clark University admission application (Common Application, or Coalition Application with Scoir) - there is no application fee.
A separate essay submitted for Global Scholars Program Scholarship consideration.
Transcript(s) covering the last three years of education, submitted in English with certified translations where applicable.
Two letters of recommendation - one from a school counselor and one from a teacher (two academic teachers where there is no counselor).
Proof of English language proficiency if English is not your native language (TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo English Test or Pearson PTE).
International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form, available only after the admissions application is submitted.
Optional interview - optional but strongly encouraged, and for international students it can also be used as a supplementary measurement of English proficiency.
documents: Common Application or Coalition Application with Scoir submission (no application fee)
Separate essay for Global Scholars Program Scholarship consideration
Transcript(s) covering the last three years of education, in English (certified translations accepted)
Counselor and teacher letters of recommendation
Official TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Pearson PTE score report
International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form (from the Applicant Status Portal)
selection_criteria: Consideration is given to students who have demonstrated exceptional academic performance and personal qualities during their secondary school years.
Merit-based scholarship decisions are solely based on information presented in the admission application without consideration of financial need.

We seek students who want to be involved and are community-oriented, and those who believe that through bettering themselves, they are responsible for improving their lives, environment, systems, and tools.
Your English proficiency will be assessed holistically, considering your scores, transcript, essay, and letters of recommendation.
For the Presidential Scholarship only: finalists are selected and invited to interview.
coverage: Clark publishes no breakdown of what the Global Scholars Program Scholarship covers. Its only published coverage statements for international aid are: 'Each year a select number of first-year and transfer international students receive merit scholarships and need-based grants to attend Clark' and 'We are not able to offer financial assistance to cover the full cost of attendance.'

For context, the only international-eligible award with published coverage is the Presidential Scholarship, which covers full tuition plus on-campus housing and meals for all four years - and Clark notes recipients still face roughly $12,000-$15,000 of additional costs per year.
application_method: Submit the Clark University admission application through the Common Application (or Coalition Application with Scoir) by the Early Action / Early Decision I deadline of November 1 or the Regular Decision / Early Decision II deadline of January 15.
Submit the separate essay required for Global Scholars Program Scholarship consideration - there is no separate scholarship application form.

Complete and submit the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form, which becomes available on the Applicant Status Portal only after the admissions application is submitted.
Optionally sit for an in-person or virtual interview, or submit one through InitialView or Vericant.
official.application_route: Apply to Clark through the Common App (or Coalition App with Scoir, no fee) by the November 1 or January 15 admission deadline, submit the separate Global Scholars essay, and complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form on the Applicant Status Portal - no separate scholarship application exists.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants who are not U.S. citizens and not U.S. permanent residents (green card holders) - Clark's definition of an international student. No residency requirement beyond that.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. This award is exclusively for international students as Clark defines them: applicants who do not hold U.S. citizenship and do not hold U.S. permanent residency. It is listed among the five merit scholarships open to international first-year students.
official.description: Clark lists the Global Scholars Program Scholarship as one of five merit scholarships open to international first-year applicants, and it is one of only two (with the Presidential Scholarship) for which a separate essay is required rather than automatic consideration. Clark gives no award amount, currency, period, duration or coverage detail for this scholarship anywhere on its current financial assistance pages, so it should be read as an unquantified merit reduction toward the cost of attendance rather than a fundable figure.
official.program_type: Merit-based university scholarship for international first-year undergraduates (essay-required track)
official.english_requirement: If English is not your native language, an official TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo English Test or Pearson PTE score report is required. Clark states it has no specific minimum scores and gives these general indicators: TOEFL iBT 85 overall with no sub-score below 20 (or 4.5 overall with no sub-score below 4 on the new scoring scale as of January 2026); IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-score below 6; Duolingo 120 overall with no sub-score below 100; PTE 61 overall with no sub-score below 55; PEXT 71 overall with no sub-score below 65. Proficiency is assessed holistically, and Clark may recommend its English for Academic Success Program (1-4 semesters) instead of direct degree entry.

verification.notes: Checked Clark's own clarku.edu pages only: the international financial aid FAQ, the international Apply for Financial Aid page, the international undergraduate admissions page, the main Apply page with the admissions-rounds table, and Cost and Financial Aid with the 2026-27 cost of attendance. Clark names the Global Scholars Program Scholarship and its separate-essay requirement on the live FAQ page, but no live Clark page publishes an amount, period, duration or coverage for it - the 'First-Year Scholarships for International Students' page that once carried the international merit scholarship detail has been retired (it now redirects to the financial aid home page), and even its last live version described only the Presidential Scholarship. Aggregator sites quote a $15,000-$25,000 range, but those figures are not on Clark's domain and were deliberately not recorded. Also flagged: the current International Financial Assistance pages state the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form is the only acceptable aid application and that Clark does not require the CSS Profile, while the undergraduate international admissions page still directs applicants to file the CSS Profile.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a scholarship you apply for directly - it rides on your Clark first-year admission application, and the separate essay is the only thing that distinguishes it from the three international merit awards everyone gets considered for automatically. No live Clark page publishes a dollar amount, currency, period or duration for it, so treat it as an unquantified merit reduction rather than a figure you can build a budget around. Plan your finances using Clark's own numbers instead: total cost of attendance of roughly $82,753 for 2026-27, with international students typically paying about $40,000 per year after scholarships and aid. Because admissions are explicitly need-aware, your family's ability to pay can influence the decision itself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International first-year applicants who are strong, distinctive essayists with a genuine global or community-engagement story, and whose families can still cover the large residual cost after Clark's merit and need-based aid.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you fall inside Clark's definition of international (no U.S. citizenship, no green card) before relying on this award at all

Start the Global Scholars essay early - it is the single element that separates this track from the three automatically-considered awards, and essays written after the deadline are the most common way to lose consideration
Assemble three full years of transcripts plus certified English translations, and line up a counselor and a teacher recommender, before the round deadline
Book an interview (in-person, virtual, InitialView or Vericant) - it is optional but strongly encouraged, and for international applicants it doubles as supplementary evidence of English proficiency
Sit TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or PTE early enough that official scores arrive before you apply; note Duolingo results must be sent from the Duolingo portal itself

Submit the Common App first, then open the Applicant Status Portal and complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form immediately - it does not exist until after you apply
Ask finaid@clarku.edu to confirm which financial form is required this cycle before paying for a CSS Profile submission, given the conflicting guidance on Clark's pages
common_rejection_risks: Omitting the separate essay - automatic consideration covers only three of the five international merit scholarships, so a missing essay takes this one off the table entirely

Triggering the need-aware rule: Clark states it will deny an application on financial grounds if the certification form shows more need than it can meet, so a large funding gap can sink an otherwise strong file
Submitting only two years of transcripts - Clark says outright that it cannot review an application with two years of credentials
Applying Regular Decision while assuming early-round funding levels - Clark states Early Decision applicants get access to more scholarship funding and a higher admission rate
Budgeting against an amount quoted by scholarship listing sites; Clark itself publishes no figure, so any number you plan around is unverified
Counting on-campus work as a funding source - Clark describes such income as 'pocket money' only and notes international students cannot work off campus
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Clark's published 2026-27 total billed charges are $77,970 (tuition $62,070, standard double room $8,580, standard board $5,780, activity fee $460, orientation fee $400, health and wellness fee $680) plus a transportation allowance of $250 and estimated books of $900, miscellaneous $800 and health insurance of $2,833, for total estimated costs of $82,753. Clark states international students typically pay around $40,000 per year after scholarships and aid, against a total cost of attendance it puts at approximately $85,000 per year - so the majority of the cost is very likely to remain with you.
document_audit: Transcripts must span the last three years of education - Clark specifically calls out applicants from systems such as China's 6-3-3, where a middle-school transcript covering the equivalent of 9th grade is needed in addition to two years of secondary school
Everything must be in English; originals plus certified translations are accepted, so budget translation time for non-English records
Duolingo scores must come directly from the Duolingo portal, while TOEFL, IELTS and PTE can be accepted as scanned copies from you or your counselor - do not assume one rule covers all four

The International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form only becomes available after you submit the admissions application, so it cannot be completed in advance and will land in your queue at the busiest moment
Two recommendations must be one counselor and one teacher, or two academic teachers if your school has no counselor - two teachers when a counselor exists does not meet the stated pattern

The financial form conflict is real: Clark's international financial aid pages say the certification form is the only acceptable application and that the CSS Profile is not required, while the undergraduate international admissions page still tells applicants to file the CSS Profile - confirm in writing before spending money on a CSS submission
alerts: No published amount: Clark's live pages give no figure for this scholarship, so treat every dollar amount circulating elsewhere as unverified and do not build a funding plan on it

Some Clark pages are stale - the international financial aid deadline table is still labelled 'fall 2025 admission' even though the dates recur each cycle, and the transfer-fall window differs between pages (February 1 - May 1 on the aid pages versus February 1 - June 1 on the Apply page)
Admission is need-aware, so an honest large financial need is not neutral here - it can be the reason an otherwise admissible applicant is denied
Applying Early Decision is binding (you must withdraw other applications if admitted) even though it carries more scholarship funding; Early Action is the non-binding way to reach the November 1 date

English requirements are indicators, not guarantees - meeting them does not secure admission, and Clark can instead place you in the English for Academic Success Program for 1-4 semesters before degree study
If you are a United World College graduate, a separate Davis UWC need-based grant of up to $15,000 per year may apply on top of merit consideration - worth raising with your admissions counselor
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Common App (or Coalition with Scoir) application plus the Global Scholars essay by the November 1 or January 15 deadline, then the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form appears on the Applicant Status Portal and is completed there; the admission decision and any merit award are released together (late December for Early Decision I, mid-January for Early Action, early March for Early Decision II, late March for Regular Decision).
